name: Fionnuala Deschamps-Chukwu
description: The preeminent holographic installation director of her generation, Deschamps-Chukwu creates large-scale public holographic works that occupy the boundary between entertainment and civic architecture. Of Irish-Martiniquais-Igbo heritage, she operates as a licensed independent — technically unaffiliated but dependent on corporate permits for public space access, a tension that defines her practice. Her installations have appeared in Tier 3 transit corridors, Tier 2 market halls, and twice, controversially, in Shelf underpass spaces without permits.
cultural_impact: She is credited with making holographic public art politically legible to working-class audiences, demonstrating that the medium could function as testimony rather than spectacle.
story_hooks: She has been commissioned by a Tier 5 patron for a major installation — and the commission comes with conditions about what the work cannot depict that she is considering accepting anyway.
The embedded projectors from the Ward Nine installation are still partially active in the Shelf infrastructure and have started displaying imagery she did not program.
A corporate security contractor is quietly building a case that her unpermitted installations constitute property damage — the charge carries a sentence that would include mandatory BCI modification.
